sections.h2: How can a Davie homeowner sell and walk away?
sections.html:
Three routes exist in Davie: hire an agent, sell without one, or take a cash purchase with no repairs on your side. Which one fits depends on the work the house needs and how soon the money matters.

Davie is a town in Broward County, and it behaves differently from the beach cities to the east. Its own history is tied to ranching, citrus and horses. If your lot has a barn, fencing, a pool or other outbuildings, those extras shape what an inspector will flag, so plan for them from the start.

  • Agent route: the biggest audience, plus showings, an appraisal and a loan contingency.
  • Owner route: you draft the contract, give disclosures and coordinate the closing.
  • Cash route: no lender involved, common for inherited, rented or worn-out houses.

sections.h2: Where does Davie, FL get its western character?
sections.html:
Davie was incorporated on November 16, 1925, and the town marked its centennial with events from November 2024 through 2025. Early in the twentieth century it was known as Zona, settled by workers who were draining the Everglades, and it took its present name in 1916 from the developer R.P. Davie.

Agriculture shaped it from there. The Town describes Davie as a ranching and western-lifestyle community with horse trails, an annual rodeo and a western-themed downtown. The Old Davie School Historical Museum, built in 1918, is the oldest permanent school building in Broward County, and the Orange Blossom Festival began in 1937 to honor the local citrus industry.

The heritage reaches into the rulebook. The Town publishes a Western Theme Design Manual meant to preserve citrus, cattle, equestrian and rodeo heritage, so check with the Town on whether it touches exterior work on your parcel, particularly inside the western-themed district.

sections.h2: How big is Davie and who lives there?
sections.html:
The Town of Davie says it is home to more than 107,000 residents, and it describes a rural atmosphere, a western-themed district and a large educational complex as the traits that set it apart from other Broward municipalities.

Two sellers on opposite sides of town can face very different sales. A home on a half-acre lot with an equestrian setup is priced and marketed differently from a townhome in a planned community. Roof age, pool condition and any outbuildings are worth sorting out before showings.

If an association covers your property, ask for its governing documents early. In many communities a sale needs association approval, estoppel letters and a check for pending special assessments, and a slow reply can stall a closing longer than any repair.

sections.h2: Can you rent out a Davie house as a vacation rental instead?
sections.html:
Yes, but Davie regulates it through a registration program. Under the Town Code (Chapter 16, Article IX) and section 509.242 of the Florida Statutes, a vacation rental is a unit rented to transient guests more than three times in a calendar year for periods under thirty days, or one that is advertised as regularly rented that way.

The Town requires a license from the state Department of Business and Professional Regulation before it will accept the application. The packet also asks for proof of ownership from the Broward County Property Appraiser, corporate documents if an entity owns the home, interior and exterior sketches, a Department of Revenue registration and a Broward tourist tax number.

sections.h2: Which Davie offices and records will you need?
sections.html:
Three sources cover most of what a Davie seller needs. The Town's Police Code Compliance Division, at 1230 South Nob Hill Road, handles vacation rental registration and code questions, and its number is 954-693-8237. The Broward County Property Appraiser's website, BCPA.net, is where the Town expects owners to pull proof of ownership. If an LLC or corporation holds title, the Town asks for corporate documents from Sunbiz.org.

Gather those before a buyer's attorney asks. A clean ownership record, a current tax bill and written confirmation that no code case is open make a Davie contract easier to sign, and they are quick to collect when you know where each one lives.

Disabled veterans have one more item to keep handy. The Town's rental program requires a DD214 and disability documentation to apply a veteran exemption, and the same paperwork helps if a buyer asks about the state's assessment reduction for disabled ex-servicemembers.

sections.h2: What do Broward County property taxes mean for a Davie seller?
sections.html:
Your Davie property is valued and billed by Broward County on a state-set calendar: valuation on January 1, a proposed-tax notice in August and bills in November.

  • March 1 is the filing date for exemptions and classifications, which matters for a lot with an agricultural classification.
  • The clerk takes value petitions during the 25 days after the August notice.
  • Early payment discounts start at 4 percent in November and end at 1 percent in February.
  • Delinquency begins April 1.

Assessed value on non-homestead property may climb at most 10 percent a year, the state says. Homesteads have the Save Our Homes cap instead, set at 3 percent or the inflation change, whichever is lower. The cap ends at sale, and the buyer begins at just value.

If part of your land holds an agricultural classification, ask the property appraiser how a sale or change in use affects it before you commit to a contract.

sections.h2: What will the Davie deed transfer involve?
sections.html:
The Broward clerk handles recording, and Florida's deed stamp tax is 70 cents on each $100 of consideration. The statute counts any mortgage or encumbrance on the land, assumed or not, so paying off a loan does not shrink the base as sellers sometimes hope.

Revenue officials say every party shares liability for the tax whoever agrees to bear it. Your contract assigns the cost, and the title company usually collects it.

Recording fees come on top. Section 28.24 prices the first page at $5.00 and later pages at $4.00, plus per-page records-fund and technology charges. Spousal homestead deeds and divorce deeds for the marital home carry listed exemptions, so ask the title agent before assuming tax applies.

sections.h2: What if the Davie house is inherited, facing foreclosure or rented?
sections.html:
Florida law gives each of these a defined path, and a sale stays possible.

When an heir sells, the department lists a personal representative's deed under a probated will as not taxable. Transfers made for estate planning are taxable, because it says no specific exemption covers them. Florida collects no estate tax for deaths after December 31, 2004.

After a foreclosure judgment the clerk's sale must fall 20 to 35 days later unless the plaintiff agrees to extend it. A buyer who closes sooner pays the lender and leaves the owner whatever equity remains.

Unpaid rent calls for a written three-day demand, not counting weekends and court holidays. A tenant raising any defense besides payment must deposit the rent with the court within five days or give up those defenses.

faqs.q: Does Davie require registration for short-term rentals?
faqs.a: Yes. The Town runs a vacation rental registration program tied to Chapter 16, Article IX of its code, and it asks for a state DBPR license first. Contact the Police Code Compliance Division at 954-693-8237 before advertising.

faqs.q: What is the Davie vacation rental fee?
faqs.a: A full registration year runs $500 and the half year from April 1 runs $300. Renewals cost $450 when the owner does not live there and $400 when the owner does.

faqs.q: Who records a deed for a Davie property?
faqs.a: The Broward clerk records it and takes the deed stamp tax of 70 cents per $100, and the title company usually arranges both.

faqs.q: What happens to my property tax benefit when I sell in Davie?
faqs.a: The cap ends with the sale, and the buyer is assessed at just value the next January 1. Buying another Florida homestead? Ask the Broward appraiser about portability.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Davie house with tenants still living there?
faqs.a: Yes. A buyer may accept the lease as written. For a vacant house, a monthly tenancy ends on 30 days' notice, and only a sheriff can physically remove an occupant.
